title: Unexpected SSE connection close: automated recovery & telemetry runbook
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Summary: A production customer reported a wave of sessions where Server-Sent Events (SSE) connections closed unexpectedly mid-response. Clients observed truncated transcripts (final tokens missing) and inconsistent retry behavior across SDK versions. This ticket scopes investigation, short-term mitigations, and a long-term automated recovery and telemetry plan to eliminate blind spots for future escalations.

Scope: Hosted API (primary), but fixes should be applicable to Dedicated and Private where appropriate configuration differs (idle timeout, LB behavior).

Goals: 1) Ship a minimal, low-risk mitigation to reduce customer-visible truncation within 48 hours. 2) Add per-session telemetry and correlation keys so we can reconstruct dropped sessions without customer artifacts. 3) Implement a deterministic fallback that can return a full non-stream response when streaming fails mid-request. 4) Author an on-call runbook for escalations and customer communications.
comments: 2026-02-21 - Maya Chen: Incident reported by AcmeMedia (high-traffic media summarization). They saw ~0.4% of sessions cut at token boundaries after 120s of streaming. Customer provided two example request IDs and a partial transcript. Escalation opened with SEs.

2026-02-22 - Arjun Patel: Reproduced failure in staging by simulating an abrupt TCP RST from the LB after 90-140s. Observed server-side write errors but no durable session record in current ephemeral session store. SDKs without idempotency token re-request caused duplicate or missing tails on retry.

2026-02-24 - Infra (Elena): Found idle connection timeouts on some edge tier instances (envoy 1.24 config drift). Workaround: increase keepalive and align timeouts across edge and origin; rolling fix scheduled but will not fully prevent client network flakiness.
2026-03-01 - Maya: Decided on three-track plan: (A) telemetry/diagnostics, (B) short-term fallback mitigation, (C) long-term session checkpointing. Prioritized A+B for immediate shipping.

2026-03-03 - Arjun: Drafted schema for new telemetry keys: session_correlation_id, last_emitted_token_index, last_emitted_token_checksum, socket_close_cause. Added initial Kibana queries and Grafana panel for dropped-stream rate by region.

2026-03-05 - Eng PR review: PR #6218 adds a soft flush hook that attempts a synchronous completion path when the streaming channel errors before EOS. Risk: slightly higher tail CPU. Mitigation: gated by per-customer rate and feature flag.

2026-03-08 - QA (Nina): End-to-end tests created to simulate LB resets, client-initiated aborts, and SDK retry sequences. Found an edge case where the non-stream fallback returned a slightly different tokenization cause; added normalization to ensure deterministic token boundary handling.

2026-03-10 - Customer Success: Communicated temporary mitigation and offered a short-term config change (increase client keepalive and SDK upgrade). Customer accepted canary change on 10k sessions/day.
2026-03-12 - Arjun: Merged telemetry and fallback feature flags to staging. Runbook draft completed. Long-term checkpointing design moved to follow-up ticket ENG-555002.
Action items: finalize rollout plan, coordinate Infra config sync, run canary for 72h, prepare postmortem template for customer communication.
playbook_steps: Triage: capture request IDs and sample transcripts from customer and mark urgent
Mitigation: enable feature flag 'sse-sync-fallback' for affected customer(s) and increase server-side keepalive for their region
Diagnostics: collect session_correlation_id, last_emitted_token_index, last_emitted_token_checksum and socket_close_cause from logs for each affected request
Reconstruction: use telemetry to determine whether the missing tail is available on origin; if present, trigger async backfill to customer (via non-stream response endpoint)
Escalation: if >0.2% sessions truncated for a single customer over 24h, escalate to oncall SRE + platform reliability
Rollback: disable 'sse-sync-fallback' and revert keepalive adjustments if CPU or error budgets exceed thresholds in canary
acceptance_criteria: Canary: deploy fallback feature to 3 customers with total ≤250k streaming tokens/day and observe <0.05% truncated streams after 72h
Telemetry: logs must include session_correlation_id and last_emitted_token_index for 100% of streaming sessions in staging
SDK: released patch for JS/Go SDK to include idempotency token and improved retry guidance
Runbook: oncall runbook reviewed and sign-off by SE and SRE
testing_plan: Unit and integration tests for soft-flush path and checksum verification
Chaos tests that inject RST/FIN at different offsets during streaming to validate deterministic fallback
Load test with synthetic customers to verify CPU/Tail impact of fallback under peak load
Canary rollouts in 3 regions with traffic steering and automated health gates
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Synchronous fallback increases CPU/tail latency on origin. Mitigation: gate by customer-level rate, circuit-breaker, and telemetry-based auto-disable.
Risk: Telemetry volume increases log ingestion cost. Mitigation: sample non-incident sessions at 5% and full capture for flagged failures.
Risk: Inconsistent tokenization between stream and non-stream paths. Mitigation: normalization and checksum-based matching before backfill.
Risk: Private/Dedicated deployments may not receive a hosted config change. Mitigation: publish configuration guide and a lightweight migration script for customers running Private
postmortem_notes: Root cause hypothesis: a subset of edge proxies had stale idle-timeout configs combined with intermittent client-network resets leading to abrupt socket closures. The platform lacked durable per-session emission checkpoints to reconstruct missing tails.
Customer impact: AcmeMedia reported partial transcripts affecting downstream analytics for 14k requests; remediation reduced visible truncations by estimated 90% during canary.
Follow-ups: implement persistent ephemeral-session snapshots (ENG-555002), standardize LB keepalive across fleet (ENG-556000), and add SDK onboarding docs for recommended keepalive/heartbeat settings
